facts.text: Bainbridge was platted in 1805 by General Nathaniel Massie and incorporated as a village in 1838, named for naval hero Commodore William Bainbridge.
The village’s Harris Dental Museum, housed in an 1815 brick house, is listed on the National Register and preserves the birthplace of America’s first dental school.
Bainbridge’s early economy grew around a grist mill, distillery, and small furnace built by Massie, leveraging the fertile lands along Paint Creek.
By the late 1800s, Bainbridge became a shipping point on the Dayton, Toledo & Ironton Railroad, boosting local farming and small‑scale manufacturing.
The village’s founding reflected patriotic sentiment, as Massie chose higher ground to avoid malaria reported at his earlier settlement, Amsterdam.
